# The leakage-only adversary (generated by experiments/measure_leakage_only_adversary.py)

Evidence data/processed/evidence_full_v4, label selection data/processed/label_selection/better_v2_full_v4.parquet, graph data/processed/graph_full_neuronal_split_binders_drugs_v4_enzymes; 20 pseudo-draws of the item 25 rule at the registered held-out fraction, 1000 bootstrap resamples per reading.

The adversary knows two things: which training perturbations share a seed node with the held-out perturbation, and the training labels. No edge, no propagation, no descriptor. It is handed the leaked labels directly, so its advantage is an upper bound on what any model could take from this channel by lookup. A held-out perturbation with no leaked neighbour takes the training base rate, which keeps the advantage a measure of the leak rather than a mixture of a leak and a handicap.

Read against H1's registered requirement of a 0.05 macro and micro difference, and against the measured precision of the readings (paired-bootstrap 95 percent half-widths of 0.019 to 0.063 macro and 0.018 to 0.041 micro, growing by about 1.4 at Holm's smallest level).

## The channel this does not cover

Two perturbations sharing a seed node perturb the same node, so a label transfers by identity and a lookup substitutes for mechanism: that is the channel measured here. Two perturbations whose seeds sit in one pathway are the hypothesis under test rather than a leak, so transfer along a route is not measured and must not be: bounding it would bound the study's own subject. A channel outside both descriptions is a disclosed limitation.
